states.message: Welcome to Fraud detection! Please select a topic you would like to learn about.
Watch for gold-plated fakes, tungsten-filled items (right weight, wrong purity), and borrowed jewelry pledged by someone who isn't the true owner.
Inconsistent purity readings, tampered hallmarks, or a customer who's unusually anxious about the appraisal process are all worth a second look.
Photocopied IDs presented as originals, mismatched photos, or documents with altered dates are common red flags — always verify against the original document.
If you suspect fraud, don't confront the customer — quietly escalate to your branch manager or the compliance team and hold the transaction.
